study type: Observational study comparing two distinct time periods (pre-pandemic vs. early pandemic)
exposure: COVID-19 pandemic mitigation measures and their associated socioeconomic and psychological crisis
cohort: Pregnant women in Uruguay who delivered within the first 6 months of 2019 (pre-pandemic) or the first 6 months of 2020 (early pandemic period without maternal infections), differentiated by public and private healthcare systems.
finding: In the public healthcare system, COVID-19 mitigation measures were associated with a significant increase in the risk of low birth weight and the composite outcome (preterm birth or low birth weight), while no significant changes were observed in the private system.
cross-section timing: Data was collected for the first 6 months of 2019 (pre-pandemic) and the first 6 months of 2020 (early pandemic phase).
